name: Monthly Ticket Volume & Trends
description: Monthly aggregated ticket volume across all historical periods. Identifies peak creation months, intake spikes, and seasonality.
aliases: in which month created more tickets
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) RETURN t.created_at.year AS year, t.created_at.month AS month, count(t) AS volume ORDER BY volume DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.created_at.month = 8 AND t.created_at.year = 2026 RETURN t.category AS category, t.priority AS priority, count(t) AS volume ORDER BY volume DESC LIMIT 10

name: Ticket Volume
description: Count of tickets created in a period; optionally breakdown by channel, priority, or Queue.
search_text: Ticket Volume Count of tickets created in a period; optionally breakdown by channel, priority, or Queue. tickets created case volume intake volume new tickets volume created how many tickets intake new tickets (Ticket)-[:in_queue]->(Queue) (Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(Contact) (Tenant)-[:HAS_TICKET]->(Ticket)
aliases: how many tickets created in august
in which month created more tickets
disambiguation: NOT Conversation Volume (CCAAS). Ticketing work items are Ticket nodes.
business_rules: Filter by Ticket.created_at with datetime($period_start) / datetime($period_end)
Group by Ticket.channel property or (Ticket)-[:in_queue]->(Queue)
Person path: (Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(Contact)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) RETURN t.channel AS channel, count(t) AS volume ORDER BY volume DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id WITH coalesce(t.channel, 'Unknown') AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: How many tickets were created this week?

name: Open Tickets
description: Tickets whose status is open or active. In the graph, tickets are labeled :Ticket with property t.status.
search_text: Open Tickets Tickets whose status is open or active. active tickets unresolved tickets open cases backlog open tickets how many open ticket are present now how many open tickets are there (:Ticket)
disambiguation: NOT Conversation volume (CCAAS). Use Ticket + Ticket.status. DashboardMetrics.open_tickets is a cached snapshot — prefer live Ticket count for accuracy.
business_rules: Tickets are labeled :Ticket with string property t.status.
Open tickets count: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE toLower(t.status) = 'open' RETURN count(t) AS open_tickets.
Active backlog: toLower(t.status) IN ['open', 'pending', 'reopened'].
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE toLower(t.status) = 'open' OR 'OpenTicket' IN labels(t) RETURN count(t) AS open_tickets
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE toLower(t.status) = 'open' WITH t.priority AS dimension, count(t) AS count RETURN dimension, count ORDER BY count DESC
keywords: how many open tickets are there
how many open ticket are present now
examples: How many open tickets do we have?
how many open ticket are present now?
how many open tickets are there ?

name: Overdue Tickets
description: Non-terminal tickets whose resolution deadline (Ticket.due_at) is before now. due_at is computed from SLA by priority at create/update.
search_text: Overdue Tickets Non-terminal tickets whose resolution deadline (Ticket.due_at) is before now. due_at is computed from SLA by priority at create/update. past due tickets SLA overdue missed due date late tickets overdue past due late missed deadline due_at (:Ticket) (Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(SLA) (Tenant)-[:HAS_DASHBOARD_METRICS]->(DashboardMetrics)
disambiguation: Different from CCAAS SLAInstance.breached_at. Ticketing overdue uses Ticket.due_at on the Ticket node, optionally linked via GOVERNED_BY to SLA.
business_rules: Overdue = due_at < datetime() AND status not terminal
Join (:Ticket) WHERE is_terminal = false
Optional: (Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(SLA) for policy hours by priority
DashboardMetrics.overdue is cached snapshot
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE toLower(t.status) = 'overdue' OR 'OverdueTicket' IN labels(t) OR (t.due_at IS NOT NULL AND t.due_at < datetime() AND t.status <> 'Resolved') RETURN count(t) AS overdue_tickets
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE toLower(t.status) IN ["open", "pending", "reopened"] AND t.due_at IS NOT NULL AND t.due_at < datetime() AND t.organization_id = $organization_id OPTIONAL MATCH (t)-[:in_queue]->(q:Queue) RETURN coalesce(q.queue_name, 'Unqueued') AS dimension, count(t) AS overdue ORDER BY overdue DESC LIMIT 10
examples: Which queue has the most overdue tickets?

name: Resolved Tickets
description: Tickets that reached a terminal status; prefer Ticket.resolved_at or Ticket.status.is_terminal = true.
search_text: Resolved Tickets Tickets that reached a terminal status; prefer Ticket.resolved_at or Ticket.status.is_terminal = true. closed tickets solved tickets resolution volume resolved closed solved resolution count (:Ticket) (Ticket)-[:resolved_by]->(Agent) (Ticket)-[:assigned_to]->(Agent)
business_rules: Resolved when resolved_at IS NOT NULL OR (Ticket)-[:USES_STATUS]->(Ticket.status {is_terminal: true})
Filter period on resolved_at
Resolver (L2) via (Ticket)-[:resolved_by]->(Agent); L1 via ASSIGNED_TO
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE toLower(t.status) = 'resolved' OR 'ResolvedCase' IN labels(t) RETURN count(t) AS resolved_tickets
examples: How many tickets resolved this week?

name: Reopened Tickets
description: Tickets currently or historically in Reopened status (non-terminal). Indicates resolution quality issues.
search_text: Reopened Tickets Tickets currently or historically in Reopened status (non-terminal). Indicates resolution quality issues. reopen rate came back open reopened cases reopened reopen came back (:Ticket) (AuditEvent)-[:ON_TICKET]->(Ticket)
business_rules: Status key often 'Reopened' with is_terminal = false
Prefer (:Ticket) WHERE status = 'Reopened'
Audit trail may show status transitions in AuditEvent.meta
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE toLower(t.status) = 'reopened' RETURN count(t) AS reopened_tickets

name: Ticket SLA Compliance
description: Proportion of support tickets that met their SLA resolution deadline or first response deadline. Breached tickets are labeled :BreachedCase and resolved tickets are labeled :ResolvedCase, linked via (:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(:SLA).
search_text: Ticket SLA Compliance Share of tickets that met resolution deadline or first response deadline. SLA met rate within SLA SLA adherence on-time resolution SLA compliance within SLA breach on time (:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(:SLA) (:Ticket:BreachedCase) (:Ticket:ResolvedCase)
disambiguation: CCAAS SLA breach uses SLAInstance.breached_at. Ticketing uses Ticket.due_at / first_response_at vs SLA.
business_rules: Tickets are labeled :Ticket. Breached tickets also carry the label :BreachedCase; resolved tickets carry :ResolvedCase.
Relationship to policy: (:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(:SLA).
Resolution SLA met: NOT "BreachedCase" IN labels(t), or t.resolved_at <= t.due_at.
Resolution breached: "BreachedCase" IN labels(t).
SLA compliance rate = toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN NOT "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / count(t).
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(s:SLA) RETURN s.priority AS priority, count(t) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS breached, sum(CASE WHEN NOT "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS met, toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN NOT "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / count(t) AS sla_compliance_rate ORDER BY priority
examples: What is our ticket SLA compliance?
How many tickets breached SLA this week?
why the sla rate is droped?
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(s:SLA) WITH s.priority AS priority, count(t) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS breached, toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) / count(t) AS breach_rate RETURN priority, total, breached, count(t) - breached AS met, breach_rate ORDER BY breach_rate DESC

name: Ticket SLA Rate
aliases: why the sla rate is droped
description: Proportion of support tickets that breached SLA resolution or response deadlines. Breached tickets carry the label :BreachedCase and are linked to their SLA policy via (:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(:SLA).
business_rules: Tickets are labeled :Ticket. Breached tickets also carry the label :BreachedCase; resolved tickets carry :ResolvedCase.
Relationship to policy: (:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(:SLA) where SLA has priority (urgent, high, medium, low), resolution_hours, and first_response_hours.
Breached ticket count: count(t:BreachedCase) or sum(CASE WHEN "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END).
SLA breach rate = toFloat(breached_tickets) / count(t).
Breakdown dimensions: s.priority, t.queue_name, t.category, t.channel, t.assignee_name.
examples: why the sla rate is droped?
what is the sla breach rate for tickets?
which priority has the highest sla breach rate?
search_text: Ticket SLA Rate why the sla rate is droped sla drop SLA rate Ticket SLA Breach Rate Breached tickets Ticket SLA Support SLA Ticket SLA Compliance BreachedCase (:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(:SLA) (:Ticket:BreachedCase)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(s:SLA) RETURN s.priority AS priority, count(t) AS total_tickets, sum(CASE WHEN "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS breached_tickets, toFloat(sum(CASE WHEN "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))/count(t) AS breach_rate ORDER BY breach_rate DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(s:SLA) WHERE (t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end)) OR (t.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($compare_end)) WITH s.priority AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) AND "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($compare_end) AND "BreachedCase" IN labels(t) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous, count(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 END) AS current_total, count(CASE WHEN t.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 END) AS previous_total RETURN dimension, current, previous, (toFloat(current)/CASE WHEN current_total=0 THEN 1 ELSE current_total END - toFloat(previous)/CASE WHEN previous_total=0 THEN 1 ELSE previous_total END) AS delta ORDER BY delta DESC

name: Ticket Queue Assignment & Routing
description: How tickets are assigned and routed to support queues based on ticket category, issue type, and domain via (:Ticket)-[:in_queue]->(:Queue).
search_text: Ticket Queue Assignment & Routing how the tickets assigned to queue how are tickets routed to queue ticket routing rules queue assignment queue routing logic (:Ticket)-[:in_queue]->(:Queue)
aliases: how tickets are assigned to queue
how the tickets assigned to queue
business_rules: Tickets are classified by category and domain, then routed to specialized queues via (:Ticket)-[:in_queue]->(:Queue).

Each queue has a specific operational scope defined by Queue.description and Queue.queue_name (e.g. Shipping & Delivery Support, Order Management & Fulfillment, Returns & Refunds Support, Payments & Billing Support, Product Support, Customer Account & Access Support, Offers & Loyalty Support).
Ticket.queue_name denormalises the assigned queue name directly on the Ticket node.
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:in_queue]->(q:Queue) RETURN q.queue_name AS queue, q.description AS scope, count(t) AS ticket_count ORDER BY ticket_count DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:in_queue]->(q:Queue) RETURN t.category AS category, q.queue_name AS queue, count(t) AS count ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 10
keywords: how the tickets assigned to queue
how are tickets assigned to queue
examples: how are tickets routed to queues?
what are the rules for queue assignment?

name: Ticket Agent
description: Agent is the ticketing workforce bridge to Employee (IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR). Handles tickets via ASSIGNED_TO (L1) and RESOLVED_BY (L2).
search_text: Ticket Agent Agent is the ticketing workforce bridge to Employee (IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR). Handles tickets via ASSIGNED_TO (L1) and RESOLVED_BY (L2). support agent ticketing assignee resolver case agent ticket agent assignee resolver Agent who is assigned (Agent)-[:IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR]->(Employee) (Ticket)-[:assigned_to]->(Agent) (Ticket)-[:resolved_by]->(Agent) (Queue)-[:HAS_MEMBER]->(Agent) (Tenant)-[:HAS_TICKET_AGENT]->(Agent)

business_rules: (Agent)-[:IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR]->(Employee)
(Ticket)-[:assigned_to]->(Agent) for L1
(Ticket)-[:resolved_by]->(Agent) for L2
(Queue)-[:HAS_MEMBER]->(Agent)
For display name use Employee via IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR, not a name property on Agent
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:assigned_to]->(ta:Agent)-[:IS_TICKET_AGENT_FOR]->(u:Employee) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN u.first_name + ' ' + u.last_name AS agent, count(t) AS assigned_count ORDER BY assigned_count DESC LIMIT 10
examples: Which agent has the most assigned tickets?

search_text: Unassigned Tickets Open tickets with no L1 assignee (no ASSIGNED_TO Agent, or assignee_id null). no assignee unclaimed tickets tickets without agent unassigned no assignee unclaimed who owns (Ticket)-[:assigned_to]->(Agent) (:Ticket) (Tenant)-[:HAS_DASHBOARD_METRICS]->(DashboardMetrics)

search_text: Due Today Tickets Open tickets whose due_at falls on the organization's local calendar today (OrgSettings.display_timezone). tickets due today due date today deadline today due today deadline today due_at today (:Ticket) (Tenant)-[:HAS_ORG_SETTINGS]->(OrgSettings) (Tenant)-[:HAS_DASHBOARD_METRICS]->(DashboardMetrics)

name: Ticket First Response Time
description: Time from ticket creation to first staff response (Ticket.first_response_at). SLA target hours come from SLA.first_response_hours by priority.
search_text: Ticket First Response Time Time from ticket creation to first staff response (Ticket.first_response_at). SLA target hours come from SLA.first_response_hours by priority. FRT time to first reply first response SLA speed to first answer first response FRT response time reply speed (Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(SLA) (Ticket)-[:assigned_to]->(Agent)
disambiguation: CCAAS uses Conversation.first_agent_response_at / SLAInstance. Ticketing uses Ticket.first_response_at and SLA.
business_rules: FRT seconds = duration.between(created_at, first_response_at).seconds
Only tickets with first_response_at IS NOT NULL
Met SLA if first_response_at <= created_at + SLA.first_response_hours (via GOVERNED_BY)
Average FRT = avg(duration) over period
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.first_response_at IS NOT NULL AND t.first_response_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.first_response_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN avg(duration.between(t.created_at, t.first_response_at).seconds) AS avg_first_response_seconds

name: Ticket Resolution Time

search_text: Ticket Resolution Time Duration from Ticket.created_at to Ticket.resolved_at for resolved tickets. time to resolve average resolution time ART handle time ticket resolution time time to resolve ART how long to close (Ticket)-[:has_sla]->(SLA) (Ticket)-[:resolved_by]->(Agent) (Ticket)-[:assigned_to]->(Agent)

ART = avg(duration.between(created_at, resolved_at).seconds)

cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND t.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN avg(duration.between(t.created_at, t.resolved_at).seconds) AS avg_resolution_seconds

name: Ticket CSAT
description: Customer satisfaction on tickets: Ticket.csat_score (1–5) and csat_rated_at. Supports average, promoter/detractor rates, and response rate among resolved.
search_text: Ticket CSAT Customer satisfaction on tickets: Ticket.csat_score (1–5) and csat_rated_at. Supports average, promoter/detractor rates, and response rate among resolved. customer satisfaction CSAT score satisfaction rating survey score CSAT satisfaction rating promoter detractor survey (Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(Contact)
business_rules: Rated tickets: csat_score IS NOT NULL
average_csat = avg(csat_score) where rated
Promoter: csat_score >= 4; Detractor: csat_score <= 2; Neutral: = 3
Response rate = rated among resolved / resolved (resolved_at IS NOT NULL)
Customer-level CSAT: (Contact)<-[:OVERLAY_OF]-(SupportProfile)<-[:REPORTED_VIA]-(Ticket)
Do NOT invent a Customer node — Customer is Contact sublabel when contact_type = customer
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.csat_score IS NOT NULL AND t.csat_rated_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.csat_rated_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN avg(toFloat(t.csat_score)) AS average_csat, count(t) AS rated_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(sp:SupportProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(ct:Contact) WHERE t.organization_id = $organization_id AND t.csat_score IS NOT NULL AND t.csat_rated_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.csat_rated_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN ct.cdp_id AS contact, avg(toFloat(t.csat_score)) AS avg_csat, count(t) AS ratings ORDER BY avg_csat ASC LIMIT 10

business_rules: (SupportProfile)-[:OF_ACCOUNT]->(ClientAccount)
(Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(SupportProfile)
Do not confuse ClientAccount with Account (CRM) or Tenant (accounts.organizations)
cypher_template: MATCH (t:Ticket)-[:REPORTED_VIA]->(sp:SupportProfile)-[:OF_ACCOUNT]->(ca:ClientAccount) WHERE ca.organization_id = $organization_id AND ca.name = $account_name RETURN count(t) AS ticket_count, avg(CASE WHEN t.csat_score IS NOT NULL THEN toFloat(t.csat_score) END) AS avg_csat

name: Global Cypher Query Contract
description: Mandatory rules the Cypher agent must apply to EVERY generated query against the Worktual OKG. Retrieve and prepend this card on every request.
business_rules: CASE SENSITIVITY: Neo4j labels, relationship types and property names are case-sensitive. Labels are PascalCase (Conversation, SalesOrder, ContactProfile). Relationship types are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT, BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT). Properties are lower_snake_case (created_at, churn_score, total_amount). Never title-case a property, never PascalCase a relationship, never UPPER a label.

NODE KEYS ARE NOT ALWAYS 'id'. Registry: Contact=cdp_id, CustomerScore=cdp_id, ContactPoint=identity_id, Insight=insight_id, Recommendation=recommendation_id, Segment=segment_id, Order=order_id, OrgProfile=organization_id, KnowledgeOrgProfile=organization_id, AssignmentSettings=organization_id, WebchatChannelConfig=channel_config_id, SocialChannelConfig=channel_config_id, Product=id (bigint), PlatformProduct=id (string). Every other label uses id.

ANCHOR BOTH ENDS WITH LABELS. These relationship types are overloaded and reused across unrelated pairs: CONTAINS, HAS_LINE, FOR_PRODUCT, FOR_CONTACT, FOR_OPPORTUNITY, FOR_ACTIVITY, FOR_ACCOUNT, OWNED_BY, CREATED_BY, ASSIGNED_TO, IN_QUEUE, FROM_QUEUE, HANDLED_BY, OFFERED_AGENT, FOLLOWS_HOURS, USES_TEMPLATE, APPROVED_BY. Never write (a)-[:CONTAINS]->(b) without labels on both a and b.

TENANT SCOPE IS THE DATABASE. Each tenant has its own Neo4j database. Do NOT add `WHERE n.organization_id = $organization_id` unless the runtime actually binds $organization_id — an unbound parameter makes Neo4j throw 'Expected parameter(s)' and the agent returns an error instead of an answer.

DATETIME vs DATE. Most timestamps are ZONED DATETIME (UTC) and must be compared with datetime($period_start). But DATE-typed columns must be compared with date($period_start): Invoice.issue_date, Opportunity.expected_close_date, Contact.acquisition_date, Contact.date_of_birth, Holiday.holiday_date, Quote.valid_until. Mixing date and datetime raises a type error.

DURATIONS. Use duration.inSeconds(a, b).seconds for elapsed time. duration.between(a, b).seconds returns ONLY the seconds component (excludes days/months) and silently under-reports any span longer than 24 hours.
ALWAYS BOUND BOTH ENDS OF A PERIOD: `>= datetime($period_start) AND < datetime($period_end)`. A start-only filter makes 'this week' silently mean 'this week and everything after'.
GUARD DIVISION: CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE toFloat(numerator)/total END. A bare toFloat(x)/0 returns null and the answer reads as 'unknown'.
EXISTENCE CHECKS: use EXISTS { (c)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer) } or COUNT {}. Bare pattern expressions outside WHERE are removed in Neo4j 5.

NEVER INVENT A TENANT FAN-OUT EDGE. The following (Tenant)-[...]->(x) relationships are commented out in core.yaml and DO NOT EXIST in the graph: HAS_CONTACT, HAS_CONTACT_PROFILE, HAS_CONVERSATION, HAS_INTERACTION, HAS_DEAL, HAS_DEAL_ACTIVITY, HAS_COMPANY, HAS_COMPANY_SITE, HAS_QUOTE, HAS_PROPOSAL, HAS_INVOICE, HAS_SALES_ORDER, HAS_CONTRACT, HAS_NOTIFICATION, HAS_MISSED_CONTACT, HAS_SHARED_NOTE, HAS_KNOWLEDGE_DOCUMENT, HAS_QUOTE_TEMPLATE, HAS_PROPOSAL_TEMPLATE, HAS_INVOICE_TEMPLATE. Match the label directly instead: MATCH (d:Opportunity) — not MATCH (:Tenant)-[:HAS_DEAL]->(d:Opportunity), which returns zero rows.

(Contact)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(Conversation) DOES NOT EXIST. Conversations, interactions, activities, insights and recommendations hang off a Contact through synthetic collection nodes. See concept_contact_history.
IF NO CARD MATCHES, SAY SO. Do not improvise labels or relationship types that are absent from these cards.
